title: Bug: [Trixie] Some timezones not settable due to tzdata update
author: benle7
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

The test of test_clock.py::test_config_clock_timezone fails with the following errors:
ERR timedatectl[120334]: Failed to set time zone: Invalid or not installed time zone 'PST8PDT'
ERR hostcfgd: ['timedatectl', 'set-timezone', 'PST8PDT'] - failed: return code - 1, output:#012None

**Observation:**
/usr/share/zoneinfo/PST8PDT is missing on the Trixie image,
but appears in 'timedatectl list-timezones'.
In the master image, the /usr/share/zoneinfo/PST8PDT exists.

**tzdata** package version (dpkg -l | grep tzdata):
master: 2025b-0+deb12u2
Trixie: **2025b-4+deb13u1**

**Root Cause:**
The tzdata package was updated in the Trixie image (2025b-4+deb13u1).
According to the tzdata NEWS file:
**https://sources.debian.org/src/tzdata/2025b-4%2Bdeb13u1/NEWS**
"This affects only the legacy zones EST5EDT, CST6CDT, MST7MDT, **PST8PDT**, CET, MET, and EET, which previously used nonzero types for these timestamps."

The update removed or changed the structure of legacy POSIX zone files like PST8PDT.
timedatectl CLI requires a real zoneinfo file to set /etc/localtime, so it now fails.

**Flow:**
1. tests/clock/test_clock.py:ClockUtils.get_valid_timezones:
show clock timezones
2. src/sonic-utilities/show/main.py:timezones:
timedatectl list-timezones
3. This will list all timezones, including legacy entries like PST8PDT.
4. tests/clock/test_clock.py:test_config_clock_timezone:
config clock timezone PST8PDT
5. src/sonic-host-services/scripts/hostcfgd:DeviceMetaCfg:timezone_update:
timedatectl set-timezone PST8PDT
6. Error: Invalid or not installed time zone 'PST8PDT'

### Steps to Reproduce

Option 1: Run test_clock.py::test_config_clock_timezone
Option 2: config clock timezone PST8PDT
Option 3: timedatectl set-timezone PST8PDT

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual Behavior:
ERR timedatectl[120334]: Failed to set time zone: Invalid or not installed time zone 'PST8PDT'
ERR hostcfgd: ['timedatectl', 'set-timezone', 'PST8PDT'] - failed: return code - 1, output:#012None

Expected Behavior:
Timezone update passed successfully.


### Relevant log output

```shell
ERR timedatectl[120334]: Failed to set time zone: Invalid or not installed time zone 'PST8PDT'
ERR hostcfgd: ['timedatectl', 'set-timezone', 'PST8PDT'] - failed: return code - 1, output:#012None
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell

```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

comments.author: tjchadaga
comments.body: @benle7 - could you file this under sonic-mgmt and see if a test change is more suitable?

comments.author: benle7
comments.body:
@tjchadaga 
I'm not sure if this is a test issue.

As I described above, the test calls the following SONiC CLI:
show clock timezones

Then, in src/sonic-utilities/show/main.py:timezones, it executes the following Linux command:
timedatectl list-timezones

The test logic selects one option from this list at random.

The issue is that 'PST8PDT' exists in the list, even though there is no corresponding file:
/usr/share/zoneinfo/PST8PDT
So, it cannot be set.

linkedPullRequests.title: Install tzdata-legacy to allow using legacy timezones from timedatectl
linkedPullRequests.author: saiarcot895
linkedPullRequests.body:
Fixes #24562

#### Why I did it

The tzdata package has moved the legacy/deprecated timezone names into a separate package called tzdata-legacy. However, the version of systemd in Trixie doesn't filter out timezones that are listed in zone.tab, but not actually physically present on the device, resulting in an error if those timezones try to get set.

Debian bug: https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=1124737

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**:

#### How I did it

As a workaround, install the tzdata-legacy package to make all timezones that are listed in timedatectl work.
